## Discover real guest reviews to help you choose the perfect stay in Marbella

How are reviews collected?

Philip H.

Guest verified by HomeToGo

We had a fantastic stay and would happily return. The apartment was spotlessly clean, modern, and had everything we needed for a relaxing holiday. The Wi-Fi and air conditioning worked perfectly throughout our stay, and the beds were incredibly comfortable. Our favourite part was the balcony overlooking the beautiful gardens – it was a lovely place to sit with a coffee in the morning or a drink in the evening, with plenty of comfortable seating. The pool area was also excellent, with crystal-clear water and a peaceful atmosphere, so we spent lots of time relaxing there. Although it’s a little further from Puerto Banús than where we usually stay, we actually enjoyed the quieter location. It was an easy walk to Puerto Banús, the beach, Nueva Andalucía and San Pedro, and taxis back in the evening were quick and inexpensive. Overall, a brilliant apartment in a peaceful setting, and we’d highly recommend it to anyone visiting Marbella.

Frederic B.

Guest verified by HomeToGo

We rented the villa for one week as a group of 16 people and had a wonderful stay. The villa offers plenty of space and, overall, matches the description very well. Located slightly outside the center and up on a hillside, the property benefits from a pleasant breeze — a real blessing in the summer heat. One of the highlights was that there were truly enough seating and lounging options for everyone, both indoors and outdoors, which is not always the case in large group accommodations. A major positive was the excellent on-site support. The local team was always available, incredibly responsive, and solved any request or issue right away — we felt really well taken care of. A supermarket is about a 10-minute walk away, although the way back is uphill. The beach can also be reached by foot in around 15 minutes. By car it’s quicker, but parking near the beach can be a bit tricky. Overall, we had a fantastic time and would definitely recommend this villa for large groups.

Guest verified by HomeToGo

Exactly like the photos. The house and complex were very clean and very well maintained. We had a private booking with Seaview Home, in the house in the picture. They were so helpful. We were there for 2 months in the low season, it was lovely and quiet. I think it would be very busy in the summer. Great parking short walk to supermarket or local restaurant. The on-site restaurant was not open until the last week of March. Easy walk to busses if needed. Receptionists were very helpful if needed. The gym and indoor pool were very good and the gym was well equipped. Would highly recommend for a couple, as it’s one bedroom with very comfortable bed loads of towels, in fact everything you need. The staff at Seaview Home were amazing. Wi-Fi was very good, and they even made sure we had English TV while we were there.

## Yachts, history and beauty in Marbella

### Marbella Harbour

The Marbella Harbour, popularly known as Puerto Banús **,** is considered to be the most exclusive harbour in the Málaga area. Luxurious yachts moor here surrounded by a wining and dining experience which attracts celebrities and royalty alike.

### Marbella Old Quarter

As its name suggests, the Marbella Old Quarter is the original town with many traditional buildings and narrow, winding cobbled streets. In the area you will find boutique shops, quaint art galleries, pubs and restaurants.

### Alameda Park

Located to the south of the Marbella Old Quarter is Alameda Park. This small park is a tranquil place to relax and view the many beautiful tropical plants on display. In the heart of the park is a magnificent fountain, decorated with colourful, traditional Andalusian tile-work, and decorated benches for a well-deserved break.

### Avenida del Mar

The Avenida del Mar is a pedestrian street connecting the Marbella Old Quarter and the Golden Mile beach. As you head down through the Alameda Park to the beach, you will encounter an open air art gallery displaying ten surrealistic sculptures by the Spanish artist **Salvador Dalí**.

### Iglesia Mayor de la Encarnacion

The Iglesia Mayor de la Encarnacion, or Church Of The Incarnation, is a major attraction for visitors to Marbella. Located next to the castle, the church, built in 1505, is a mixture of Renaissance, Gothic and baroque styles and is home to the Lady of Solitude statue.

- Which top landmarks you shouldn't miss in Marbella?



You definitely want to check out the Old Town, also called the Casco Antiguo, which is full of charming whitewashed buildings and narrow streets. The Plaza de los Naranjos is a beautiful square in the heart of the Old Town. And don't forget to see the iconic Marbella Church, Iglesia de la Encarnación, with its beautiful bell tower.

- What are the best short term rentals in Marbella?





Among the short term rentals in Marbella, [Aqua Apartments Bellamar - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/59815754), [Marbella Village](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/39405576) and [Ona Marbella Inn](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15500256) are the most popular ones.

- What kind of weather can travelers expect in Marbella?



Marbella has a Mediterranean climate with warm, sunny summers and mild, wet winters. Expect average highs in the 80s during the summer and lows in the 50s during the winter. You'll get plenty of sunshine year-round!

- What are the best short term rentals with a pool in Marbella?





[Aqua Apartments Bellamar - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/59815754), [Ona Marbella Inn](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15500256) and [Ona Alanda Club Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15504796) are the best short term rentals with a pool in Marbella.

- Are there any famous stadiums or sports arenas in Marbella?



Marbella doesn't have any major stadiums or sports arenas. But there are many smaller sports venues and facilities, including the Marbella Football Center, a popular training ground for professional soccer teams.

- What are the best short term rentals with a jacuzzi in Marbella?





The best short term rentals with a jacuzzi in Marbella are [Aqua Apartments Bellamar - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/59815754), [Ona Alanda Club Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/15504796) and [ÁTico En Apartahotel - Marbella](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/marbella-short-term-rentals#cp:details/1227671).

- What notable natural landmarks are near Marbella?



Marbella is right on the Costa del Sol, so you're surrounded by beautiful beaches. But for something different, head to the Sierra Blanca mountains, which are just a short drive away. You'll find hiking trails, stunning views, and even the famous La Concha mountain peak.

- What are the best short term rentals for families and kids in Marbella?

- What part of Marbella is ideal for finding lodging?



The most popular areas for lodging are the Golden Mile, which is known for its luxury hotels and villas, and Puerto Banús, a glamorous marina filled with shops, restaurants, and nightlife. But you can also find great options in the Old Town, which is more charming and traditional.

### [Long Term Rentals Set for a Comeback on the Costa del Sol and Marbella](https://marbellalongtermrentals.com/en/news/long-term-rentals-comeback-marbella/ "Long Term Rentals Set for a Comeback on the Costa del Sol and Marbella")

Over the past decade, the Costa del Sol—particularly Marbella—has become a magnet for both tourists and investors. With its enviable Mediterranean climate, luxury lifestyle, and strong international appeal, property demand has surged across the board. In recent years, however, the long-term rental market faced increasing pressure. Rising prices and a preference for short-term holiday lets created a tight market, limiting mobility for locals and long-term residents.
But that tide is turning.
A Changing Legal Landscape for Holiday Rentals
In 2024, the Spanish government introduced a series of new regulations aimed at tightening control over the short-term rental sector. These laws include stricter licensing requirements, limitations on the number of days properties can be rented out short-term, and increased oversight on platforms like Airbnb and Booking.com.
For property owners, these changes are already having an impact. Many are reconsidering the long-term benefits and stability that come with traditional lets, especially as bureaucracy around holiday rentals grows more complex.
Long Term Rentals Regaining Momentum
At Marbellapads.com, we’ve noticed a clear uptick in both enquiries and listings in our Long Term Rentals department. The shift isn't just legal—it's practical. Landlords are increasingly seeking the predictability of year-round tenants over the seasonal volatility of the holiday market.
At the same time, renters who had been priced out or discouraged by limited availability are now finding renewed hope. With more properties returning to the long-term market, there’s a wider selection at more competitive rates than we’ve seen in recent years.
Why This Matters for Tenants and Landlords
For tenants, this means better opportunities to secure high-quality, long-term accommodation in key areas of the Costa del Sol, from Nueva Andalucía to Estepona. Stability, value, and choice are all improving.
For landlords, the current climate presents a chance to rethink investment strategies. Long-term lets offer consistent income, fewer management headaches, and now—with increased regulation in the short-let sector—less administrative burden.
The Role of Marbellapads.com
As one of the leading Long Term Rental specialists on the Costa del Sol, we are uniquely positioned to guide both tenants and property owners through this evolving market. Whether you’re looking to rent your property out for the long term or searching for your next home in Marbella, our experienced team is here to help you navigate with confidence.

### [UK Expats and the Long Term Rentals market in Marbella](https://marbellalongtermrentals.com/en/news/uk-expats-long-term-rentals-marbella/ "UK Expats and the Long Term Rentals market in Marbella")

Over the past five years, Marbella's long-term rental market has undergone significant transformations, particularly affecting British residents. These changes have been driven by factors such as Brexit, evolving tax regulations, and shifts in property market dynamics.
Brexit and Residency Implications
The UK's departure from the EU has introduced new residency requirements for British nationals in Spain. Previously, UK citizens enjoyed freedom of movement within the EU, allowing for extended stays without additional paperwork. Post-Brexit, non-EU citizens, including Brits, are limited to stays of 90 days within any 180-day period without a visa. Those wishing to reside longer must apply for appropriate visas, such as the non-lucrative visa for retirees or the work visa for employment purposes. This added bureaucracy has influenced some British nationals to reconsider long-term stays in Marbella.
Taxation Changes for Property Owners
Tax regulations have also shifted. Non-EU residents who rent out property in Spain are now subject to a higher rental income tax rate of 24%, up from the previous 19%. Additionally, they can no longer deduct expenses related to the rental property, impacting the profitability for British landlords.
Evolving Rental Market Dynamics
Marbella's rental market has experienced notable changes. A significant number of property owners have transitioned from long-term to short-term rentals, attracted by higher profitability from tourist lettings. This shift has led to a reduced supply of long-term rental properties, driving up prices. Currently, a well-furnished two-bedroom apartment in a desirable Marbella location rents for between €1,400 and €3,000 per month.
Impact on British Residents
These developments have presented challenges for British residents seeking long-term rentals in Marbella. The combination of stricter residency requirements, increased tax burdens, and rising rental costs has made securing affordable long-term accommodation more complex. Some British expats have opted to purchase properties to bypass rental market challenges, while others have chosen to return to the UK or explore alternative destinations.
Looking Ahead
Despite these challenges, Marbella continues to attract British residents drawn to its climate, lifestyle, and amenities. Prospective long-term renters are advised to stay informed about residency and tax regulations, explore various visa options, and consider engaging local experts to navigate the evolving rental landscape effectively.

[The Long Term Rental Market in Marbella and Estepona](https://marbellalongtermrentals.com/en/news/the-rental-market-marbella-and-estepona/ "The Long Term Rental Market in Marbella and Estepona")

### [The Long Term Rental Market in Marbella and Estepona](https://marbellalongtermrentals.com/en/news/the-rental-market-marbella-and-estepona/ "The Long Term Rental Market in Marbella and Estepona")

The long-term rental markets in Marbella and Estepona have experienced significant transformations recently, characterized by escalating rental prices, constrained supply, and shifting property owner preferences.
Rising Rental Prices
In Marbella, long-term rental prices have surged, with rates reaching approximately €19.2 per square meter per month. This means a well-furnished two-bedroom apartment in a desirable location can command monthly rents between €1,400 and €3,000. Similarly, Estepona has witnessed a dramatic increase in rental costs. Over the past decade, the monthly rent for an 80-square-meter apartment has escalated from €446 in 2014 to €1,297 in 2024, marking a 190% rise.
Supply Constraints and Owner Preferences
A notable shift among property owners from long-term to short-term rentals has further tightened the availability of long-term rental properties. This transition is driven by the higher profitability associated with short-term tourist accommodations. Consequently, the limited supply has intensified competition among prospective tenants, contributing to the upward pressure on rental prices.
Impact on Local Residents
The surge in rental prices and limited availability have posed challenges for local residents, particularly those with moderate incomes. In areas like the Costa del Sol, including Marbella and Estepona, high rental costs have made it difficult for local workers to secure affordable housing. Many are compelled to seek accommodations farther from their workplaces, leading to longer commutes and increased living expenses.
Contributing Factors
Several factors have contributed to the current state of the long-term rental market:

Tourist Demand: The popularity of Marbella and Estepona as tourist destinations has led property owners to favor short-term rentals, which offer higher returns during peak tourist seasons.

Regulatory Environment: While there have been regulatory efforts to control the proliferation of short-term rentals, enforcement challenges remain. Increased scrutiny of platforms like Airbnb and Booking.com aims to ensure compliance with licensing requirements.

Economic Factors: Rising property values and the appeal of real estate investment in these areas have attracted both domestic and international investors, further driving up housing costs.

Future Outlook
The long-term rental markets in Marbella and Estepona are expected to remain competitive. Prospective tenants should anticipate continued high rental prices and limited availability. Engaging with local real estate professionals and exploring emerging neighborhoods may provide opportunities to secure suitable accommodations.
